report.summary: The api-gateway p99 spike (1633 ms at 20:00:00Z, back to about 178 ms by 20:05:00Z) coincides with slow responses on the gateway's /api/v1/search route (885 to 1079 ms WARNs from 19:42 to 20:03). Gateway CPU, memory, error rate and request rate stayed flat, and no changes were recorded in the 19:00-20:30 window. The likely origin is the search path (search-service or its search-index dependency), but search-service metrics and logs were unavailable and search-index is unmonitored, so the root cause is not established. The only recent change to search-service is v5.3.1 deployed 2026-09-08, about 47 hours earlier, which does not match the onset. Confidence is low and the incident is not conclusive.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: A transient slowdown in the search index (e.g. a maintenance or rebuild job) raised search-service response times, so gateway calls to /api/v1/search exceeded 0.9 to 1.1 s and pushed the gateway's p99 to 1.6 s for one interval before recovering.
assumptions: search-index causes the slowdown, since search-index has no telemetry.
The gateway's p99 spike is caused by the search route alone.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: The v5.3.1 query parser change from 2026-09-08 added latency to some search queries, which surfaced as slow upstream calls on /api/v1/search during this window.
assumptions: The regression is load- or input-dependent and only appeared at 19:40 to 20:05.
The deploy was not already visible in the 47 hours before the incident.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: A transient gateway-side issue (e.g. connection pool or retry behaviour on the search route) produced the slow-upstream warnings and p99 spike without a backend fault.
assumptions: The gateway's own resource metrics are too coarse to show a short pool exhaustion.

observed_facts.statement: api-gateway latency_p99_ms jumped to 1633.34 ms at 2026-09-10T20:00:00Z; all other 5-minute points from 19:00 to 20:30 are between 173 and 187 ms.
Gateway logs show WARN 'upstream response slow' on route /api/v1/search at 19:42:27 (885 ms), 19:59:08 (892 ms), 20:01:12 (1072 ms) and 20:03:10 (1079 ms).
Gateway error_rate (0.34 to 0.45%), request_rate (407 to 435 req/s), cpu_pct (36.5 to 39.5%) and memory_pct (50.5 to 54.0%) show no step change during 19:00 to 20:30.
Two WARN 'rate limiter: client near burst limit' messages appeared at 19:50:21 and 20:16:01, outside the spike window except as background.
The only search-service change in the last 7 days is deploy v5.3.1 ('query parser fixes') completed at 2026-09-08T20:30:00Z.
Health checks for api-gateway, search-service, search-index, auth-service and checkout-service were all HTTP 200 at 20:28:00Z, after the spike ended.
Past incident P02 (2026-02-27) had the same symptoms: search p99 high and gateway 'slow upstream' warnings, caused by an index rebuild during peak traffic.

assumptions: Health checks are shallow and do not exercise search queries, so healthy checks do not rule out a search-path slowdown.
The /api/v1/search route's slowness is caused by search-service or search-index rather than by the gateway itself.
The 5-minute metric resolution may hide the exact duration of the spike.
The 'retention gap' on search-service metrics is a telemetry gap, not evidence of no problem.
(unverified - no valid evidence cited) No change events were recorded for api-gateway, search-service or the wider system between 19:00 and 20:30 on 2026-09-10.

(unverified - no valid evidence cited) search-service metrics query returned 'retention gap' and its log queries timed out after 3 attempts, so search-service telemetry for the incident window is unavailable.
(unverified - no valid evidence cited) search-index has no metrics or logs in the telemetry store.

inferred_conclusions.statement: The incident is a transient latency spike on the search path, most likely originating in search-service or search-index, not in the gateway's own resources.
A search-index maintenance job, such as an index rebuild as in P02, is a plausible cause, but there is no change record or telemetry to confirm it.
The search-service v5.3.1 deploy is unlikely to be the trigger, because it happened about 47 hours before onset and no change occurred in the window.
Root cause is unresolved: the search-service and search-index telemetry needed to confirm the mechanism is missing.

remediation.action: No customer-facing action is needed now; the spike self-resolved. Keep the P3 alert open for monitoring.
remediation.rationale: The gateway p99 recovered by 20:05:00Z and health checks are green.

remediation.action: Restore search-service metrics and logs and check for a search-index job (rebuild, compaction, backup) running around 19:40 to 20:05 UTC.
remediation.rationale: The data gap prevents confirming the origin of the slow responses.

remediation.action: If the spike recurs, check the search-index scheduler and move heavy maintenance off peak, as in P02.
remediation.rationale: P02 showed the same symptom signature from an index rebuild at peak.

remediation.action: Add search-index metrics and logs, and a deep health check that runs a representative search query.
remediation.rationale: Current health checks are shallow and search-index is not observable.

remediation.action: Add a per-route latency alert on /api/v1/search at the gateway, with a threshold below the global p99.
remediation.rationale: The route-level WARNs appeared about 18 minutes before the global p99 breach.

open_questions: What did search-service and search-index do between 19:40 and 20:05 UTC? Those logs and metrics timed out or are missing.
Is the 'retention gap' on search-service metrics caused by the same backend problem as the log timeouts?
Did a scheduled index job or a traffic change on the search path run in this window? No change record shows one.
Did the v5.3.1 deploy from 2026-09-08 change search latency at all, which would show as a slow build-up rather than a step?
Why did the global p99 spike to 1.6 s for one 5-minute point when the route WARNs show 0.9 to 1.1 s?
data_gaps: query_metrics(start=2026-09-10T19:30:00Z, end=2026-09-10T20:30:00Z, service=search-service) -> error: Error: metrics for search-service unavailable (retention gap)

query_logs(start=2026-09-10T19:30:00Z, end=2026-09-10T20:30:00Z, service=search-service, min_level=WARN, limit=20) -> timeout: Timed out after 10000 ms: log backend query for search-service exceeded deadline (gave up after 3 attempts)

query_logs(start=2026-09-10T19:55:00Z, end=2026-09-10T20:06:00Z, service=search-service, min_level=INFO, limit=20) -> timeout: Timed out after 10000 ms: log backend query for search-service exceeded deadline (gave up after 3 attempts)

brief.title: brief gateway latency blip
brief.alert: ALERT [P3] api-gateway p99 latency 1.6s (threshold 1.5s) for ~4 minutes around 20:00 UTC; auto-resolved at 20:05 UTC. No customer reports.
